rationale: Three of the six groups in Jesus's answer (11:5, BSB: "The blind receive sight, the lame walk ... the deaf hear") appear together in Isaiah 35:5-6: "the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. Then the lame will leap like a deer" (BSB). In the Septuagint the nouns match (typhlon, kophon, cholos against Matthew's typhloi, kophoi, choloi), and the deaf clause matches in verb as well (ota kophon akousontai against kophoi akouousin); the verbs for the blind and the lame differ. The Expositor's Greek Testament notes that kophoi means "deaf" here though "in Matthew 9:32-33, it means dumb, showing that the prophecy, Isaiah 35:5, is in the speaker's thoughts," and Meyer calls the answer an "echo of Isaiah 35:5 f." Isaiah 35:4 frames the passage as God's own coming ("your God will come ... He will come to save you," BSB), which the Cambridge Bible notes. Isaiah 29:18 also pairs the deaf hearing with the blind seeing, and Isaiah 26:19 has the dead rising, so the answer gathers language from more than one Isaiah passage; no verse in this app's Isaiah mentions lepers. Graded allusion because there is no formula; strong because three groups and one full verb-noun pairing match. This row starts from 11:5; the separate row from 9:27-33 to the same verses is graded plausible.
